title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 establishes guidelines and standards to ensure that AI systems are robust, safe, and trustworthy. It promotes research into reliable AI methods and requires oversight to prevent misuse and protect the public.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act aims to safeguard individuals from misleading AI practices by establishing strict disclosure and transparency requirements. It requires companies to clearly label AI-generated content and ensures that consumers are not tricked into thinking they are interacting with humans, thereby promoting honest digital experiences.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is a proposed law that aims to strengthen national preparedness for the risks and challenges posed by advanced artificial intelligence technologies. It focuses on establishing standards, protocols, and accountability measures so that organizations and government agencies can proactively manage and mitigate potential security threats from AI.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This act aims to protect the integrity of elections by preventing the use of artificial intelligence to deceive voters. It establishes guidelines and enforcement mechanisms to detect and mitigate AI-generated misinformation or manipulation.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act aims to strengthen national security by creating a dedicated task force to address risks and challenges associated with artificial intelligence. The act focuses on developing policies, sharing best practices, and coordinating efforts across government agencies to ensure AI technologies are safe, reliable, and aligned with U.S. interests.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 establishes standards for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks that arise from the development and use of AI systems. It also imposes security requirements and oversight mechanisms to protect against misuse, ensure transparency, and safeguard public safety.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 aims to regulate the deployment and interaction of AI-driven physical systems across industries. It establishes guidelines and coordination mechanisms to ensure safety, interoperability, and compliance with national standards.

title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to provide further transparency and accountability for the use of content that is generated by artificial intelligence (generative AI) in political advertisements by requiring such advertisements to include a statement within the contents of the advertisements if generative AI was used to generate any image or video footage in the advertisements, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The amendment would require political advertisements that use AI‑generated images or video to include an explicit disclosure stating that generative AI was used. This change aims to increase transparency and accountability in election campaigns by making such disclosures mandatory under the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law designed to safeguard the integrity of elections by limiting the use of artificial intelligence that could mislead voters or spread false information. It sets rules and penalties for creating or distributing deceptive AI content that could influence electoral outcomes.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act proposes a framework to oversee artificial intelligence systems that can autonomously enhance their own capabilities. It seeks to require transparency, safety checks, and regulatory oversight to ensure these self‑improving AIs operate safely and ethically.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act temporarily suspends the construction and operation of AI‑dedicated data centers so that lawmakers can assess their environmental, security, and economic impacts. This pause allows regulators to evaluate the risks and benefits before permitting future AI data center development.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is a proposed law designed to curb the deployment of artificial intelligence that could act without proper human oversight or control. It would require developers and operators to implement strict safety protocols, monitoring systems, and accountability measures to ensure AI technologies do not pose risks to public safety and security.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 creates a federal board tasked with overseeing and investigating the security and ethical implications of AI systems. It empowers the board to conduct audits, enforce compliance, and collaborate with industry to mitigate AI‑related cyber risks.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act seeks to ensure that artificial intelligence technologies are developed and used in ways that benefit American society. It emphasizes promoting innovation while protecting privacy, transparency, and jobs for citizens.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires Chinese companies to regularly report on the development and deployment of artificial intelligence technologies. The law aims to promote transparency, ensure compliance with national security and ethical standards, and help the government monitor AI capabilities across the country.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a proposed law that restricts the use of artificial intelligence in providing medical care, ensuring that only licensed human doctors can diagnose, prescribe, and treat patients. It seeks to protect patient safety and maintain professional standards by limiting AI’s role to supportive tools rather than autonomous decision‑makers.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This policy proposes creating a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the President’s Executive Office to monitor and address risks from AI and other emerging technologies. The office would coordinate national efforts, develop guidelines, and help mitigate potential threats to security and society.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution establishes a new Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to study the technology’s effects and help shape national policy. The committee will investigate AI developments, recommend regulations, and coordinate federal efforts to address its social, economic, and security impacts.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a legal framework for systematically assessing and mitigating risks associated with artificial intelligence systems. It requires developers, users, and regulators to conduct thorough risk evaluations and implement safeguards to protect public safety, privacy, and economic stability.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed U.S. law that aims to regulate the design, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence systems to safeguard public safety and protect individual rights. It establishes a framework for transparency, risk assessment, and oversight, setting standards for developers, users, and regulators while outlining penalties for non‑compliance.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a law that requires companies using AI to measure and reduce the environmental impact of their technologies. It sets rules for reporting, encourages greener AI practices, and imposes penalties for companies that fail to meet the standards.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to embed foundational AI knowledge into elementary through high‑school curricula so students and teachers can use and evaluate AI tools responsibly. It also sets up funding, training, and equity‑focused guidelines to help schools adopt AI technologies while protecting privacy and ensuring ethical use.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 is designed to create a national framework that ensures AI research is conducted safely, transparently, and responsibly. It sets standards for safety testing, risk disclosure, and accountability, while also providing funding and guidance to support trustworthy AI development.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: This policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security—working through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency—to create a pilot program that uses AI to protect critical infrastructure from cyber threats. It also includes additional provisions for other related purposes.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 requires public schools to incorporate AI education into their curricula, teaching students how AI works and its impact on society. It also directs federal funding for teacher training, the development of national AI standards, and tools to assess students’ AI readiness.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act sets rules for using artificial intelligence in processing Veterans Affairs claims, making sure the systems are reliable and fair. It also creates oversight and error‑correction mechanisms to protect veterans’ rights and keep the process transparent.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 seeks to make the Department of Veterans Affairs' use of artificial intelligence more transparent by requiring clear documentation and disclosure of AI systems employed in veteran services. The act aims to build trust and accountability by ensuring veterans and stakeholders understand how AI decisions impact healthcare, benefits, and other VA operations.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act establishes a national program to inform the public about artificial intelligence and its impact. It designates resources and responsibilities for educational institutions, media outlets, and government agencies to deliver clear, accessible information on AI technologies.
